name: Mauritius
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. claims.title: Known to Arab and Malay sailors
claims.summary: Mariners crossing the Indian Ocean are thought to have known the uninhabited island, reputedly recorded on Arab maps as 'Dina Arobi'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1000-known-to-arab-and-malay-sailors, claim TL:MUS:event:1000:known-to-arab-and-malay-sailors, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese chart the Mascarenes
claims.summary: Portuguese navigators sight and map Mauritius and the neighbouring islands as a provisioning stop, but found no colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1507-portuguese-chart-the-mascarenes, claim TL:MUS:event:1507:portuguese-chart-the-mascarenes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Dutch name the island Mauritius
claims.summary: Admiral Wybrand van Warwijck claims the island and names it for Maurice of Nassau, stadtholder of the Dutch Republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1598-the-dutch-name-the-island-mauritius, claim TL:MUS:event:1598:the-dutch-name-the-island-mauritius, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First permanent Dutch settlement
claims.summary: The Dutch East India Company establishes a settlement, exploiting ebony forests and introducing sugar cane and livestock.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1638-first-permanent-dutch-settlement, claim TL:MUS:event:1638:first-permanent-dutch-settlement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Extinction of the dodo
claims.summary: Hunting, deforestation and introduced animals wipe out the flightless dodo within decades of human arrival; last accepted sightings fall in the 1660s.

sources.label: The dodo bird: the real facts about this icon of extinction

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1662-extinction-of-the-dodo, claim TL:MUS:event:1662:extinction-of-the-dodo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Dutch abandon Mauritius
claims.summary: After unprofitable settlements plagued by storms, pests and disease, the Dutch East India Company leaves the island.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1710-the-dutch-abandon-mauritius, claim TL:MUS:event:1710:the-dutch-abandon-mauritius, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France claims the Isle de France
claims.summary: France takes formal possession of the uninhabited island, renaming it Isle de France; colonisation begins under the French East India Company from 1721.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1715-france-claims-the-isle-de-france, claim TL:MUS:event:1715:france-claims-the-isle-de-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: La Bourdonnais founds Port Louis
claims.summary: Governor Mahé de La Bourdonnais develops Port Louis as a fortified naval base, dockyard and capital, anchoring French power in the Indian Ocean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1735-la-bourdonnais-founds-port-louis, claim TL:MUS:event:1735:la-bourdonnais-founds-port-louis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A slave-worked plantation economy
claims.summary: Enslaved Africans, Malagasy and others are imported in large numbers to work sugar and other estates; they become the majority of the population.

sources.label: Le Morne Cultural Landscape (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1723-a-slave-worked-plantation-economy, claim TL:MUS:event:1723:a-slave-worked-plantation-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maroons of Le Morne Brabant
claims.summary: Escaped slaves take refuge on the isolated cliffs of Le Morne, later inscribed by UNESCO as a symbol of the struggle for freedom.

sources.label: Le Morne Cultural Landscape (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1761-maroons-of-le-morne-brabant, claim TL:MUS:event:1761:maroons-of-le-morne-brabant, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British capture of the Isle de France
claims.summary: After the French naval victory at Grand Port, a large British force lands and compels the surrender of the island in December 1810.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1810-british-capture-of-the-isle-de-france, claim TL:MUS:event:1810:british-capture-of-the-isle-de-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Paris confirms British rule
claims.summary: Britain retains the island and renames it Mauritius, while French settlers keep their language, laws and religion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1814-treaty-of-paris-confirms-british-rule, claim TL:MUS:event:1814:treaty-of-paris-confirms-british-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of slavery
claims.summary: Slavery is formally ended in Mauritius, freeing tens of thousands of enslaved people, followed by a transitional 'apprenticeship'.

sources.label: Le Morne Cultural Landscape (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1835-abolition-of-slavery, claim TL:MUS:event:1835:abolition-of-slavery, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indian indenture and the Aapravasi Ghat
claims.summary: Around half a million indentured labourers from India arrive through the Port Louis depot, the 'Great Experiment', reshaping the island's population.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1834-indian-indenture-and-the-aapravasi-ghat, claim TL:MUS:event:1834:indian-indenture-and-the-aapravasi-ghat, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Labour Party
claims.summary: The Mauritius Labour Party is founded, channelling demands of workers and the indentured-descended majority for rights and representation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1936-founding-of-the-labour-party, claim TL:MUS:event:1936:founding-of-the-labour-party, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chagos detached as the BIOT
claims.summary: Before independence, Britain separates the Chagos Archipelago to create the British Indian Ocean Territory, leasing Diego Garcia for a US base.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1965-chagos-detached-as-the-biot, claim TL:MUS:event:1965:chagos-detached-as-the-biot, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from the United Kingdom
claims.summary: Mauritius becomes an independent state within the Commonwealth, with Seewoosagur Ramgoolam as first prime minister.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1968-independence-from-the-united-kingdom, claim TL:MUS:event:1968:independence-from-the-united-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Diversification beyond sugar
claims.summary: An export-processing zone, tourism and financial services transform a one-crop colony into a diversified, growing economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1971-diversification-beyond-sugar, claim TL:MUS:event:1971:diversification-beyond-sugar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mauritius becomes a republic
claims.summary: The island replaces the British monarch with a Mauritian president as head of state, retaining its parliamentary democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-1992-mauritius-becomes-a-republic, claim TL:MUS:event:1992:mauritius-becomes-a-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ICJ advisory opinion on Chagos
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice finds Britain's continued administration of the Chagos Archipelago unlawful; the UN General Assembly concurs.

sources.label: 2025 treaty on the British Indian Ocean Territory / Chagos Archipelago

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Mauritius: An empty island remade by every ocean that touched it", terralore.co/country/MUS/chronicle#ev-2019-icj-advisory-opinion-on-chagos, claim TL:MUS:event:2019:icj-advisory-opinion-on-chagos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UK–Mauritius Chagos agreement
claims.summary: The two states sign a treaty recognising Mauritian sovereignty over the archipelago while leasing the Diego Garcia base to the UK for an initial 99 years.

Mauritius No. 1 (2025): Agreement concerning the Chagos Archipelago including Diego Garcia
